After travelling along the Chagres River, local guides will allow time for a swim by the waterfall before taking you to the village by raft. The waterfall's name is not specified in the itinerary.

In Tusipono, guests are welcomed with music played on drums and other instruments. A traditional lunch is served in an open pavilion, followed by an introduction to local dances, which you can join.

Local artisans offer carved cocobolo-wood objects, small sculptures made from tagua seeds, known as "vegetable ivory", and baskets woven from chunga palm fibres. Purchases are personal expenses. After the excursion, return to the hotel.

## Trails of the National Park

The route follows trails through Chapada dos Guimarães, among sandstone formations shaped by water and wind. Nearby are Cerrado vegetation, waterfalls and birds.

The walk ends at Véu de Noiva, or Bridal Veil Waterfall. You can see it from a viewing platform; swimming at the waterfall is not included in this itinerary.

On the eight-day trip, the excursion is followed by lunch at a local restaurant and a return to Park Eco Lodge.

From Bogotá, the route leads to Chicaque Park, where cloud forest covers the mountain slopes. The travel description notes a network of over 18 km of trails, waterfalls, viewpoints and a forest refuge. The park is home to seven forest types, more than 300 bird species and 20 mammal species.

Accompanied by a specialist local guide, you will walk along a selected trail to the forest refuge. The walk ends with a traditional lunch, after which private transport will take you back to your hotel in Bogotá.

The excursion lasts approximately six hours. Private transport, a Spanish-speaking guide, park admission, a guided walk, lunch and a local medical insurance card are included. Uneven trails and elevation gain require appropriate footwear and unrestricted mobility. Under the itinerary's conditions, the park can be visited between 08:00 and 16:30.

Cenotes are natural pools that held sacred significance for the ancient Maya. After stopping at a cenote, you will travel to Chichén Itzá, one of the New Seven Wonders of the World. The archaeological-site itinerary includes the Pyramid of Kukulcán, the ancient observatory and the city's principal structures.

After the guided visit, a transfer is provided to your chosen seaside hotel in Cancún.

Journey to the Caribbean. Private transfer from Mérida to Chichén Itzá and a full-day group tour.  

Duration: Full day 

• Start: 9:00 – 9:30 AM 

• Languages: English and Spanish 

Today, your journey takes you from the cultural heart of Yucatán to the turquoise shores of the Mexican Caribbean, with one last day of memorable adventures along the way. Your private driver will collect you from your hotel in Mérida and take you directly to Chichén Itzá, where you will join a group tour of this legendary archaeological site, one of the New Seven Wonders of the World. Marvel at the Temple of Kukulcán, explore the sacred cenote and walk through the Great Ball Court while discovering the secrets of this ancient Maya city. Afterwards, cool off with a swim in a nearby cenote, in refreshing, crystal-clear sacred waters hidden in the jungle. Before continuing, a delicious lunch at a local restaurant is included in the accommodation price. A short stop in the charming town of Valladolid offers a final taste of Yucatán's colonial atmosphere, ideal for a walk or a quick photograph. Your private transfer then continues to the Riviera Maya, with drop-off available in Cancún, Playa del Carmen or the town of Tulum (please note that transfers to Tulum's hotel zone are not provided). From here, enjoy some beach time at your own pace, or ask us about optional overnight extensions to your Caribbean stay. 

Highlights: 

● Private transfer from Mérida to Chichén Itzá 

● Visit Chichén Itzá, a UNESCO World Heritage Site 

● Swim in a sacred cenote and enjoy lunch. 

● Stop in the colourful colonial town of Valladolid 

● Arrive in Cancún, Playa del Carmen or the town of Tulum 

● Option to extend your stay — ask us about spending more time in the Caribbean 

Included: Transport, guided tour of Chichén Itzá, admission tickets, lunch, cenote visit, drop-off on the Riviera Maya 

Not included: Overnight accommodation, tips, personal expenses, overnight stay in the Riviera Maya (optional)
